newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RBA SAYS ITS ROLE IN GOLD PRICE FALL EXAGGERATED.
newsitem.headline: RBA SAYS ITS ROLE IN GOLD PRICE FALL EXAGGERATED.

text.p: The governor of the Reserve Bank of Australia, Ian Macfarlane, said on Tuesday that he believed the bank's role in the recent decline in gold prices had been exaggerated.

The bank announced in July that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold, two thirds of its total reserves. The announcement was widely blamed for a slump in gold prices, earning the bank the wrath of the Australian gold mining industry.

"On the sale of gold, I can understand why the gold mining industry has made a lot of noise and why they have been upset about it," Macfarlane said in response to a question after a speech to company directors here.
"I do want to say, however, that I do believe they've exaggerated the effect that we had on the market," he said.

"Certainly for two or three days the gold price fell quite a lot, but if you look at the sitation now the gold price is only slightly, in U.S. dollars, it's only slightly below the point where we made our announcement," he said.
Macfarlane said gold was trading around US$332 an ounce when the bank made the announcement of the gold sale. This compared with a price of about $328 in recent days, he said.
"In Australian dollar terms, the gold price is actually higher than when we made our announcement...", he said.
"The return is actually higher than when we made our announcement about our sale," he said.
"And of course any movement that's occured in the last month is tiny compared to with what had occured over the previous 18 months when we were not involved at all."
Spot gold has been trading between $318 and $330 for much of the past month.
